title: Transport of a single commutative ring sheaf across an equivalence
statement: Let (C,J),(D,K) be small sites, A a commutative ring sheaf on J and G:Sh(J)≃Sh(K) an equivalence. There are A' on K, geometric ring data g:A→A', and a:|A'|≅g.direct(|A|), with g.inverse=G.inverse and g.direct=G.functor. The structural map is g.inverse(a.hom);ε_g(|A|) and is invertible. It satisfies all four generalized-element ring identities. No module direct image is assumed in this single-ring construction.

source.place: Tag 03CR, proof: carry along the ring sheaves; Sites, Section 00YR, Proposition 00YV, rings as sextuples.

proof.text: Regard A as an internal commutative ring using its concrete sectionwise operations. Apply finiteProductRingFunctor to G.functor, obtaining a ring object Y and its comparison d:Y→G(|A|), with explicit operation equations.
Reconstruct the ring sheaf A' on the underlying sheaf of Y with the five specified section operations and comparison q:Y→|A'|. Define a=q⁻¹;d.

Use G.inverse, G.functor and the equivalence adjunction, with structural map G.inverse(a);ε. If a generalized element has a constant or binary-operation identity in A', compose with q⁻¹ and then d to rewrite it using the transported operations. Apply the counit operation lemmas and evaluate on sections; the concrete original operations give exactly the four ring fields. The structural map is a composite of isomorphisms.

proof_origin.place: Explicit Lean construction and operation calculations, expanding the transport details omitted in Tag 03CR.

mathlib_searches.results: SheafOfModules.pushforwardPushforwardAdj, SheafOfModules.pushforward, SheafOfModules.PullbackConstruction.adjunction: these require a continuous functor of sites, rather than an arbitrary adjunction of sheaf categories.

mathlib_searches.verdict: Only scheme and continuous-site specializations were returned. Used the existing library finite-product and sectionwise constructions instead.

mathlib_searches.verdict: Use these projection identities to prove the new compatibility lemmas; no exact interface already exists.
